primitives.name: Set Attention Block
primitives.verbatim_quote: - Set Attention Block (SAB, Lee et al.): transformer encoder block WITHOUT positional encoding over the agent set → permutation equivariance (no agent ordering needed).
primitives.latex: \text{SAB}(X) = \text{MHA}(Q, K, V) \text{ where } Q = K = V = X \text{ and no positional encoding}
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'X': 'set of agent features (dimensionality D × N)', 'Q, K, V': 'query, key, value matrices (D × N)', 'MHA': 'multi-head attention operator'}
primitives.assumptions: Agent order is irrelevant; permutation equivariance holds across agent sets.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Failure when agent identities are semantically ordered or when social structure is ignored.

primitives.name: Encoder-Decoder Transformer
primitives.verbatim_quote: - Encoder: FFN + temporal positional encoding → SAB_T (temporal dynamics) → SAB_S (social interactions) sequentially decoupled (cheaper than joint temporal-social attention) → context tensor C.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'X': 'input trajectory set (D × N × T)', 'C': 'context tensor (D × N)', 'SAB_T': 'temporal SAB block', 'SAB_S': 'social SAB block', 'FFN': 'feed-forward network'}
primitives.assumptions: Temporal and social attention can be decoupled without performance degradation.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When social dependencies are strong and temporal dynamics are weak, or vice versa.

layer2.mapping: The encoder generates a context tensor that captures both temporal evolution and social influence, used by the decoder for motion prediction.
layer2.telemetry: ADE (Average Displacement Error) on motion prediction tasks

primitives.name: Conditioned Motion Prediction
primitives.verbatim_quote: - CMP tasks: predict players given ball position; predict offense given ball+defense; predict defense given ball+offense; predict ball given all players.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'P': 'predicted player set', 'C': 'conditioning set (ball or team)', 'H': 'decoder input tensor', 'X^C': 'trajectory of conditioning agents', 'X^P': 'trajectory of predicted agents'}
primitives.assumptions: Conditional inputs are available and sufficient to infer motion of target agents.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When conditioning set is insufficiently informative or when future states are highly stochastic.

The core innovation lies in SAB’s permutation equivariance, which allows modeling of unordered agent sets without positional bias. Temporal and social attention are decoupled through sequential SAB blocks, reducing computational cost while preserving expressive power. The encoder-decoder framework enables flexible motion prediction conditioned on subsets of agents, aligning with GSE’s need for scenario simulation. The mathematical formulation of SAB as MHA without positional encoding ensures that outputs are invariant to agent reordering—a critical property for modeling dynamic teams. The decoder uses cross-attention to map the learned context to predictions, enabling both unconditional and conditioned motion forecasting. This dual capability supports GSI’s probabilistic inference and GSE’s tactical simulations. Failure modes include loss of expressiveness when agent identities are crucial or when social structures are oversimplified.
